lead: A personal assistant written from scratch in Python, kept small on purpose: it talks with you on Telegram, remembers your conversations, and uses a cloud or local model. You stop opening a website to chat: the assistant is yours.
objetivo: design, install, and put to work an assistant with memory and a personality you define.

aprende.t: Design the assistant before installing it

secoes.sub: From Telegram to the model and back.

nos.detalhe: You chat on Telegram, on your phone or computer, like you would with any contact.
The bot is the entry point. You create it with @BotFather using /newbot and store the token only in .env, as you learned in step 1.

INTELECTO receives the message, combines your assistant’s personality with what it remembers about you, and puts together the request for the model. It’s small by design, so you can understand and change it.
The model generates the response. In the cloud (OpenRouter), it’s more powerful and costs money per use; locally (Ollama), it runs on your computer, if it can handle it.

secoes.volta: The response returns to the same Telegram chat
secoes.legenda: Want to see other assistant systems ready to install? The Events JARVIS section brings several together.

rolagem_fim.texto: You write in Telegram, INTELECTO combines personality and memory, the model responds, and the response returns to the same chat. It’s all yours, with the token stored in .env.

secoes.titulo: From the design to your routine

texto: Before installing, write down who the assistant is: its name, how it speaks, three things it should do every week, three things it should never do, and what it needs to remember about you.
This file answers the installation questions.

exemplo.texto: Someone else reads the file and understands who your assistant is.

texto: On Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, and choose a name and @username.

exemplo.texto: The token doesn’t appear in any file besides .env.

texto: Clone INTELECTO, export your briefing from the comparison page, and ask Claude Code or Codex to build from it and doc/intelecto.md, with tests.
Use the answers in your meu-jarvis.md. The full step-by-step guide is in lesson 4 of the step 2 course.

exemplo.texto: You send "hi" and it replies with the name and style you chose.

texto: Tell it three facts about yourself one day, then ask about them the next day in a new conversation.
Then turn one weekly task into a standing request and use it five days in a row.

exemplo.texto: Every morning, when I send "day," list my three priorities based on what I told you yesterday.

secoes.sub: Copy the template, fill it in, and only then install.

abas.rot: What you need to build it
abas.html:
1. The Telegram token (from @BotFather), only in .env.
  2. The model: cloud-based (OpenRouter) or local (Ollama).
  3. The personality: your meu-jarvis.md.

Run the same question with both and record the results in a table:

  • Response time
  • Response quality
  • Cost per use

The goal is to use your own numbers to know which model to use for what.

The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Why write the meu-jarvis.md before installing?
opcoes: Because the installation won’t work without it.
Because it defines the name, style, limits, and what to remember, and answers the installation questions.
perguntas.explica: Design comes first: with its name, style, what to do, and what never to do written down, you can answer the guided setup without improvising and have a way to check whether the assistant is right.

perguntas.p: The assistant didn’t remember what you told it yesterday. What’s the first step?
opcoes: Check the course to see how memory is stored and adjust it.
perguntas.explica: Exercise E4 says exactly this: if it doesn’t remember, check the INTELECTO course to see how memory is stored and adjust it.

perguntas.p: When does a local model (Ollama) make sense?
opcoes: When your computer can handle it and your numbers for speed, quality, and cost show that it’s worthwhile.
perguntas.explica: Make the choice based on measurements: ask both the same question, make a table with speed, quality, and cost, then decide based on your numbers.
